name: Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi receives quality standards food certification

content.title: Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi receives quality standards food certification
content.summary: Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi's Nutrition and Food Services Department has been ISO 22000:2005 Food Safety Practices/Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point Analysis Management System certified.

media.alt: Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi receives quality standards food certification

content.text: Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi's Nutrition and Food Services Department has been ISO 22000:2005 Food Safety Practices/Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point Analysis Management System (HACCP) certified, making it the first hospital-based food production and service programme in Pakistan to have been certified for specialised food safety standards. The Hospital has also been recertified under the new ISO 9001:2008 standards.

ISO certifications provide international standards for quality management systems. The ISO 22000:2005, exclusive to the food and beverage industry, promotes best food safety practices and offers a system of checks and balances at critical processing points, to control and maintain the highest food quality standards.

The recertification of ISO 9001:2008, while recognising existing quality, will help the Hospital further improve the delivery of quality care to patients by ensuring compliance with international standards for established best practices. The Quality Management System focuses on five key management areas: management responsibility, resource management, service realisation and measurement, analysis and improvement. These processes have been standardised to help the Hospital become more customer-focused, quality conscious, efficient and effective.

The Hospital in Karachi initiated its ISO 9001 Quality Management Certification process with six administrative departments in 1998, with the certification of the entire Hospital a year later in 1999. Since then, the Hospital undergoes surveillance audits annually and recertification audits every three years, ultimately benefiting the patients through constantly enhanced management processes.
